newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota denies report on shift to Canada.
newsitem.headline: Toyota denies report on shift to Canada.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp on Thursday denied a media report that it planned to shift production of its Celica models to a Canadian unit.
The Asian Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that Toyota would shift production of its Celica sports-coupe model from Japan to its Canadian plant.
"It's speculation by the paper. We have no plans for such a production shift to Canada," a Toyota spokeswoman said.

In its global plan released in June 1995, Toyota said it planned to boost production capacity at its Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada Inc (TMMC) unit in Cambridge, Ontario, to 200,000 units by 1998. TMMC produced 90,134 Corollas in 1996.
Toyota has not decided yet on additional models to be produced at the Canadian unit, the spokeswoman said.
Toyota was unlikely to produce the Celica in Canada because demand for two-door coupe models is shrinking worldwide, industry sources said.
Toyota sold 13,793 Celicas in the United States in January to November last year, down 31.9 percent.
